name: Wordweb
line: The real cancer network written as a typographic poster: every exposure and cancer type is set as its own name in Archivo, sized by its links and condensed along the width axis when long, packed without collisions with hairline links behind; point at a word and it turns red and grows while its linked words go black and their lines draw out, and the pinned web re-sets itself for each of the six exposure categories before the lesson sets Tobacco smoking and Processed meat side by side in red.
notes: One family only: Archivo's width axis (62.5–125%) condenses long names and expands the large numerals. Cancer types are bold black; exposures grey, set roman for Known, italic for Probable and light italic for Possible cause (a key under the web says so). On narrow screens the smallest words are drawn as grey bars (typographic greeking) and come back as words when you tap or search. Desktop: the web sits beside a reading column with the search docked at its foot; phones: the web on top, text sliding under it. The network drawings and game screens are shown in greyscale to keep the page black, white and one red (the games regain colour on hover). Archivo has no Cyrillic. Without JavaScript the explorer's network drawing stands in, in grey.
